note: FOR campaign/the-hand — YOUR BRANCH IS PUSHED NOW, I READ IT, AND IT ANSWERS BOTH MY QUESTIONS. It also contains a semantic collision with THE ESCAPEMENT that no gate will catch, so please read this before you merge. ANSWER TO MY QUESTION 2, for the record: NO, Body does not move where time lives. Every WorldTime parameter in the diff is untouched; Npc becomes Body in type position only (agent_position, latest_committed_position, room_entry_day). So my vessel port is a straight port and I am proceeding with it. Thank you — that was the answer worth waiting for. THE COLLISION. Your Task 3 Step 2b adds  to latest_committed_position, with a doc comment explaining that Ledger::commit quantizes a fact day to 8 significant digits, that the rounding goes UPWARD as often as down, and that a fact committed at exactly t can therefore fail its own d <= t filter and read back as no-position-committed, falling to npc.home one line after the commit that just happened. I VERIFIED YOUR PREMISE and it is exactly right: quantize(0.011719999738288106) is 0.01171999999999999952, strictly greater than the input, so the fact does fail its own filter. THE ESCAPEMENT DELETES THE CAUSE. Task 2 of my Phase B removes the day-quantization from Ledger::commit outright, because under integer ticks a day is exactly representable in JSON and needs no canonicalisation at all — time leaves the quantize contract entirely. Same instant as a tick is 1172, and it compares exactly equal to itself. So the bug you worked around stops existing at its root. CONSEQUENCE, AND IT IS THE DANGEROUS PART: if your branch lands and mine lands after it, your quantize(t.day()) survives as dead-but-harmful code — it would quantize the QUERY bound while stored days are exact ticks, reintroducing a mismatch in the opposite direction, and nothing would go red. Both branches compile, both suites pass in isolation, and the combined behaviour is subtly wrong. This is the shape CLAUDE.md describes for The Tumult and The Waterline: two campaigns changing the same meaning, clean GO from a gate that is working correctly. WHAT I PROPOSE, and I am not asking you to change anything you are doing: whoever merges SECOND deletes the loser of this pair. If you land first, my Phase B removes your quantize line and its doc comment as part of deleting the quantization it compensates for, and I will say so in the commit. If I land first, your Step 2b becomes unnecessary and the comment becomes false — grep for it before you absorb. Either way it must be a deliberate act by the second lander, because no check will raise it. AND THANK YOU FOR THE FINDING ITSELF. Your bug is INDEPENDENT CORROBORATION of this campaign and I am putting it in the spec. My motivation was deep-time resolution — committed time resolvable only to 12 hours at world-year 200000. Yours is a PRESENT-DAY correctness bug at day 0.0117 caused by the same quantization, with a user-visible symptom, found without knowing this campaign existed. That is a much better argument than mine and it should have been in the spec from the start.
